If things couldn’t get any crazier in the Pacific, Tropical Storm Co-May has made landfall directly over the city of Shanghai and is causing major freshwater flooding in Zhejiang Province, China. Over 280,000 people were reportedly evacuated from flood-prone areas. 

Co-May previously struck Luzon in the Philippines after briefly reaching Typhoon status, and the system has already claimed 26 lives.

(Radar credit: cyclonicwx)

Leaders of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints in the Philippines are continuing to monitor the impact of heavy rainfall and flooding across the country. Typhoon Co-may made landfall a few days ago, after seasonal monsoon rains and two earlier typhoons had already swamped much of the country for more than a week. 

More than 6 million people were affected by flooding, including 1.85 million families. All Latter-day Saint missionaries in the country are safe and accounted for.  

Four Church facilities in Bulacan and Pangasinan sustained damage due to heavy rain, strong winds and rising floodwaters. Several Latter-day Saint meetinghouses have opened as temporary shelters, where 400 people have sought refuge from flooded neighborhoods. 

The Church is working to donate more immediate emergency aid to those seriously impacted. Local Church leaders are also working to minister to members in need in the country.
